title: The Right Content
article_body:
## Why Most Content Does Not Work

Most businesses create content for the wrong audience. They write for casual browsers, people who are still early in their research and far from a buying decision. The result is content that gets a handful of views, generates almost no leads, and frustrates the marketing team into thinking content does not work.

Content works when it speaks to buyers, not spectators. A buyer is someone who already knows they need what you offer and is actively researching their options. They want answers to specific questions. They want to understand pricing. They want to know what can go wrong. They want to compare their options. When you give buyers exactly what they are looking for, you earn their trust before they ever contact you.

That is what The Right Content is built to do.

## The Core Frameworks in This Section

The Right Content component is built around several interconnected frameworks. Each one addresses a different dimension of how your buyers research and how you can meet them in that process.

### The Big 5

The Big 5 are the five subjects every buyer researches before making a significant purchase: cost and price, problems and concerns, comparisons and alternatives, reviews, and best-in-class options. These are the topics most companies avoid addressing publicly. That avoidance is a mistake, because buyers are going to find this information somewhere. The companies willing to address these subjects honestly are the ones that earn trust and win business.

### The Selling 7

Video accounts for over 82% of all internet traffic, and buyers increasingly turn to video to evaluate their options before making contact. The Selling 7 are seven types of videos that have a direct impact on sales: cost and price videos, 80% videos, product and service fit videos, landing page videos, customer journey videos, bio videos, and claims we make videos. Each type serves a specific function in the buyer's journey and gives your sales team tools to close deals faster.

### YouTube and Short-Form Video

YouTube is the second-largest search engine in the world. Most companies treat it as optional. Endless Customers companies treat it with the same level of strategy and commitment as their website. Short-form vertical video on platforms like Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and TikTok is a separate channel that builds brand awareness at scale. Both deserve a deliberate approach.

### AI for Content

AI tools can dramatically accelerate content production when used correctly. They help with ideation, research, drafting, and repurposing. But human oversight is not optional. Content that lacks real expertise, authentic voice, and genuine perspective will not build trust, regardless of how efficiently it was produced.

### Be More Human

As AI-generated content becomes more common, the companies that stand out will be the ones that feel most human. Personal brands matter. Behind-the-scenes content matters. One-to-one video in the sales process matters. This is the fourth pillar of becoming a known and trusted brand, and it runs through everything in The Right Content.

### Your Content Team

Outsourced content almost always misses. It lacks the expertise, the authentic voice, and the inside knowledge that only your team can provide. The most successful Endless Customers companies bring content production in-house with two dedicated roles: a content manager and a videographer. This section covers what those roles look like, what they require, and how to hire for them.

## What You Will Find in This Section

Every article in this section is designed to give you a practical understanding of one part of The Right Content framework. Start with The Big 5 if you are new to the methodology. If you already understand the written content side, move into the Selling 7 and video strategy. Wherever you are in your Endless Customers journey, this section has something actionable for you.

key_questions.question: What is The Right Content in Endless Customers?
key_questions.answer: The Right Content is the first component of the Endless Customers system. It is the practice of creating content that addresses the exact questions, fears, and concerns your buyers are already researching — particularly on topics most companies avoid, such as pricing, problems, and honest comparisons. When done consistently, this content builds trust at scale and brings buyers to you already informed and closer to a decision.

key_questions.question: What are The Big 5?
key_questions.answer: The Big 5 are the five content categories every buyer researches before making a significant purchase: cost and price, problems and concerns, comparisons and alternatives, reviews, and best-in-class options. These topics generate more trust and more qualified leads than any other type of content when addressed honestly and thoroughly.

key_questions.question: What is The Selling 7?
key_questions.answer: The Selling 7 are seven types of videos proven to shorten sales cycles and build trust: cost and price videos, 80% videos (FAQs), product and service fit videos, landing page videos, customer journey videos, bio videos, and claims we make videos. Used as part of the sales process, they allow salespeople to have higher-quality conversations by educating prospects before the first call.

key_questions.question: How much content should a company be publishing?
key_questions.answer: A minimum of three pieces of content per week, with two additional videos published to YouTube. Consistency matters more than volume in the early stages. Building a backlog of five to ten pieces before you start publishing ensures you can maintain that cadence without interruption.

key_questions.question: Do I need a full-time content team to implement The Right Content?
key_questions.answer: Not necessarily at the start. Companies under one million in revenue often begin with a business owner or key leader doing both writing and video. Companies between one and five million typically hire one hybrid person. Above five million, the model expands to include a dedicated content manager and videographer. The goal is always to have at least one person with full ownership of content production.
